caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal Nos. 58 and 80 of 2003 with Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 1377 of 2001
lawyer:
Khandker Mahbubuddin Ahmed, Senior Advocate, (MK Rahman and M Mohsen Rashid, Advocates with him), instructed by Syed Mahbubur Rahman, Advocate-on-Record—For the Petitioner. (In Civil Petition No. 58 of 2003)

AJ Mohammad Ali, Additional Attorney-General, (Naima Haider, Assistant Attorney-General with him) instructed by Md Ahsanullah Patwary, Advocate-on-Record—For the Petitioner. (In Civil Petition No. 80 of 2003) 

M Zahir, Advocate instructed by Syed Mahbubur Rahman, Advocate-on-Record--For the Petitioner (In Civil Petition No. 1377 of 2002)

Dr Kamal Hossain, Senior Advocate, (Tanjibul Alam, Advocate (appeared with the leave of the Court) with him), instructed by Md Aftab Hossain, Advocate-on-Record—For Respondent Nos. 1-4. (In Civil Petition No. 1377 of 2002 and Civil Petition No. 58 of 2003). 

Dr Kamal Hossain, Senior Advocate (Tanjibul Islam, Advocate (appeared with the leave of the Court) with him), instructed by ASM Khalequzzaman, Advocate-on-Record—For Respondent Nos. 1-4 (In Civil Petition No. 80 of 2003) 

Not represented—Respondent Nos. 5-11. (In all the petitions)
parties:
SSA Bangladesh Ltd and another ------ Petitioners
Vs.
Engineer Mahmud-ul Islam and others ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
Md Fazlul Karim J: These petitions for leave to appeal at the instance of the respective petitioners namely, SSA Bangladesh Limited (in Civil Petition No. 58 of 2003) and the People's Republic of Bangladesh (in Civil Petition No. 80 of 2003) are directed against the impugned judgment and order dated 19-11-2002, 20-11-2002, 24-11-2002, 25-11-2002 and 26-11-2002 passed by a Division Bench of the High Court Division in Writ Petition No. 4692 of 2000 making the Rule absolute declaring the impugned letter dated 28-4-1998 as evidenced by Annexure J to the Writ Petition by which approval was given to the petitioner (in Civil Petition No. 58 of 2003) (writ-respondent No. 8 to the Writ Petition) to establish two Private Container Terminals one at Patenga, Chittagong and another at Pangaon, Dhaka was declared illegal and without lawful authority and of no legal effect and further declaring all subsequent actions on the basis of the impugned approval to be illegal, without lawful authority and of no legal effect and the observations and the findings of the High Court Division in its order dated 3-7-2002 passed in Writ Petition No. 4692 of 2000 while disposing of the writ-petitioner's application for determination of standing of writ-respondent No. 8 to be a party as respondent in the writ petition which is the subject-matter of Civil Petition No. 1377 of 2002 at the instance of the petitioner, SSA Bangladesh Limited (writ respondent No. 8) 

 2. Facts relevant for the purpose of disposal of this Rule are that a petition by way of public interest litigation at the instance of the writ-petitioner-respondents, who shared a sense of concern and mindful of the need to be vigilant to protect the Chittagong Port suffering from adverse effect by the disputed project and the impugned approval for setting up of container terminals given by the government in favour of the writ-respondent No. 8 communicated vide Memo No. MOS/8- /Chi-1/98-96 dated 28-4-1998, (evidence by Annexure J to the writ petition) which has been challenged by the writ petitioner-respondents contending, amongst others, that the approval has been given arbitrarily, without application of mind, unreasonably and against public interest as the writ petitioner apprehended that the concerned parties have been trying to procure the project for unconscionable gain by questionable means contrary to the rules, procedure and statutory rules inasmuch as the proposed container terminals, if established, would destroy the existence and functioning of the existing Chittagong Port and that the approval has been given without evaluating the past record of the writ-respondent No. 8 as to its capability of performance, financial soundness of the applicants and in the absence of the project feasibility report and that the approval has been given on an application submitted on 29-12-1997 in the name of the writ-respondent No. 8 Company (petitioner in CP Nos. 58 and 1377 of 2002), claiming to be an affiliate of Stevedoring Services of America, a USA-based company, and another local company of insignificant entity apparent from Articles of Association and without considering the application of other applicants who applied for establishment of such container terminals at the relevant time and without inviting international tender. As per provisions of the Chittagong Port Authority Ordinance, 1976 (CPA Ordinance), the approval as given is beyond jurisdiction, since Chittagong Port Authority, being authorised to give permission, has not been consulted prior to granting the impugned approval; and that there was non-application of mind on the part of the government as contemplated under the Rules of Business framed under Article 55 of the Constitution for proper exercise of executive authority, who failed to consider identification of the priority of the project, consider the commercial feasibility of the project, since not furnished, assess the financial capability of the writ-respondent No. 8 and the necessity for publication of advertisement inviting competitive bids to get best offer and thus the provisions of Articles 27 and 31 of the Constitution have been violated, and that the persons involved in processing the proposal of writ-respondent No. 8 failed to consider the decision of the Ministry of Shipping taken on 11-7-1995 for setting up of the container terminals outside the Port area by invitation of offers through notifications, to be made by the Chittagong Port Authority and that the impugned approval has been given without considering and not following the guidelines suggested for Private Sector Participation in Ports, 1997 and without collecting the information’s as recommended in the report to the World Bank in respect of the Port Privatisation and Development Project for Container Terminals at Patenga, Chittagong and that the Government acted discriminatorily in not considering the proposals submitted during the relevant period, apart from the proposals submitted subsequently, and that the Board of Investment (BOI) has also acted arbitrarily and without application of mind in giving registration to the proposed project of the writ-respondent No. 8 in a hot-haste manner. 

 3. The writ-respondent No. 1 and the writ-respondent No. 8 who are the petitioners herein contested the Rule by filing affidavits-in-opposition and supplementary affidavits thereto separately. The contents of the affidavits-in-opposition of both the writ-respondent Nos. 1 and 8 are more or less similar. Both the writ-respondents have raised objection as to the locus standi of the writ-petitioners and the maintainability of the writ petition. They asserted that the subject matter of the writ petition relates to the policy of the government hence in the absence of arbitrariness, such action is not amenable to the writ jurisdiction of High Court Division and that the government has acted in accordance with law in giving the impugned approval and that the Master Plan of CPA dated 15-5-1995 provides for establishment of container terminals at Patenga by private sector on BOT basis and that the parties who submitted proposals, failed to submit formal proposals at the relevant time, and that the writ-respondent No. 8 submitted its proposal dated 29-12-1997 to the Secretary, Ministry of Shipping and the same was duly processed and that the Ministry of Shipping received a complete proposal from the writ-respondent No. 8 in two (2) volumes, one volume under the caption "SSA Bangladesh Limited" and the other volume under the caption "Business Plan, December, 1977" containing feasibility report, guidelines and all other documents along with the application dated 29-12-1997 and that by a letter dated 14-1-1998 the Board of Investment communicated to the writ-respondent No. 8 about granting of its registration and that as per Rules of Business the summary on the project proposal of writ-respondent No. 8 was sent to the Prime Minister on 2-2-1998 for decision, who in turn ordered for scrutiny of the proposal of the Council Committee on Economic Affairs and the said Council Committee in its meeting held on 25-3-1998 thoroughly evaluated the proposal of writ-respondent No. 8 and recommended for approval by the Prime Minister and thereafter on the approval by the Prime Minister the Cabinet Division vide letter 26-4-1998 communicated the decision to the Ministry of Shipping and the Ministry who accordingly, on 28-4-1998, issued the impugned letter of approval to the writ-respondent No. 8. It is to be noted that in the Industrial Policy of 1991, the Port sector has been kept open for Private Sector investment and that the establishment of the container terminal at Patenga under the private sector on BOT basis is also included in the Master Plan of Chittagong Port for the years 1995 to 2010 AD and that in the meeting held on 13-6-1995 under the Chairmanship of the then Shipping Minister, Mr MK Anwar, it was resolved that setting up of new container terminal under private sector outside the protected Port area would be welcomed and that the approval given in favour of the writ-respondent No. 8 is not an exclusive permission and if any other company is interested to establish such project may apply accordingly which the Board of Investment may approve and that as per Rules of Business the Council Committee on Economic Affairs is authorised to approve or recommend for approval of such private foreign investment project, and that the government of Bangladesh is not at any risk in approving the project since it will not require to make any investment and hence the question of competitive bid is not relevant in the instant project, which is open and non-exclusive in nature and more terminals may be permitted to be set up, and that in the meeting of the Parliamentary Standing Committee of the Ministry of Shipping held on 1-3-1999 the issue was discussed but no recommendation has been made and that since 1998 the government has carried out either directly or through Chittagong Port Authority studies with financial assistance of the World Bank or ADB in the greater interest of the nation, specifically to facilitate smooth import and export through setting up of private container terminals and the same will be beneficial for the country and with the implementation of proposed project additional job facility will be created. The government is not required to provide any fund, asset and/or to share any natural resource with the writ-respondent No. 8 and hence, competitive bid is not relevant in this infrastructure project and that the establishment of private container terminals by the private sector is open to all and the permission given in favour of the writ-respondent No. 8 is not exclusive and any private party at any time can apply for permission to establish more private container terminals for which there is no restriction and that the approval in reference has been given under the authority vested with the government under the Foreign Private Investment (Promotion and Protection) Act, 1980 and in terms of the Board of Investment Act, 1989 and as per Industrial Policy, 1991 (as revised), and that the writ-respondent No. 8 company is a Joint Venture Company in which Orient Maritime Limited (a Bangladeshi Company) and SSA Netherland BV of the Netherlands (subsidiary of Stevedoring Services of America of USA), are the only two (2) shareholders, and that after the approval and registration of the project by the Board of Investment the Ministry of Shipping as per Rules of Business processed the application of the writ-respondent No. 8 and a Co-ordination Committee of the Ministry of Shipping in its meeting held on 6-8-1998 recommended for issuance of letter to the concerned Ministry and Agencies for allotment of required lands for acquisition of further lands in favour of the respondents No. 1; for the project and that accordingly, the Deputy Commissioner, Chittagong, initiated land acquisition proceeding and required the writ-respondent No. 8 to deposit Taka 30,47,883.94 as compensation money for acquisition of lands, and that Memorandum of Understanding has been signed for taking on lease of certain lands belonging to Bangladesh Water Development Board and that the Ministry of Shipping is examining further if more advantage from the foreign investors can be negotiated and accordingly, a committee with senior officials has been formed and that in between 21-5-2000 and 26-12-2000 the said committee of five (5) Secretaries, appointed on 14-5-1998, held 74 meetings with the writ-respondent No. 8 and other experts on the draft Agreement for implementation prepared by writ-respondent No. 8 and the result is the draft implementation agreement dated 5-3-2001, which was subsequently sent to the Ministry of Law for vetting and on receipt therefrom after vetting, the Ministry of Shipping sent the said draft implementation agreement dated 5-3-2001 to the said Committee and that thereafter the said committee was reconstituted with the six (six) Secretaries which held 7 meetings in between 2-3-2002 and 30-4-2002 and submitted its reports to the Cabinet Division with its recommendations dated 30-4-2002 and that a summary dated 4-5-2002 was then placed before the Prime Minister for approval of a proposal for constituting a negotiating committee with the aforesaid 6(six) Secretaries for getting further benefits for the country and on 14-5-2002, after obtaining, approval of the Prime Minister, the negotiating committee was formed and the said committee held meetings from 18-5-2002 to 25-5-2002 with the writ-respondent No. 8-petitioner and it has been agreed that the project will be completed under BOT basis in place of approved BOO basis and after 30 years the ownership with all assets will vest in the government and thus the original approval has been amended and, that as the matter involves national interest, the terms and conditions of the implementation agreement is being further scrutinised and is yet to be finalised and is being processed through certain stages to be agreed upon by the concerned parties. 

 4. Khandker Mahbubuddin Ahmed, the learned Counsel appearing for the petitioner in Civil Petition No. 58 of 2003, submits that the project is to be implemented entirely as Foreign Direct Investment (FDI), something the country badly needs because the project is one of infrastructure development in private sector on BOT basis in which the Government or Chittagong Port Authority had to make no investment but a profit sharing partnership and, as such, it is in the best public interest and does not need to go through a tendering process and that the project is in pursuance of  Government policies where private investment was sought for in port infrastructure and the process of sanction followed the Government rules, regulations and Foreign Private Investment (Promotion and Protection) Act, 1980 and was done in the most transparent  manner. He next submits that apart from all the revenues which will be earned as port dues, river dues, conservancy, pilotage, etc. by the Chittagong Port Authority the project sponsors will contribute royalty to the Government which would mean a huge amount in foreign exchange accruing to the national exchequer besides other revenues and that the port efficiency would also be enhanced, which, in turn, would save millions of dollars in transshipment costs, port congestion charges and other costs levied by the foreign shipping companies. He next submits that the process being continued to finalise the implementation agreement, while construing the impugned approval to set up the container terminals at Patenga and Pangaon to be anything other than a 'letter of intent' to be followed by such implementation Agreement. The learned Counsel further submits that setting up of a Container Terminal using a port at the coastline of Bangladesh for the purpose of a largesse was being given away to the petitioner so as to amount to violation of Articles 27 and 31 of the Constitution is misconceived inasmuch as 6 (six) Secretaries to the Government of Bangladesh have applied their minds to the proposal and have agreed to issue the letter of intent, sufficiently manifests that the Government is acting reasonably with application of minds. 

 8. Dr Kamal Hossain, the learned Counsel appearing for the writ-petitioner-respondents, found fault with the process of approval of the project as arbitrary and unreasonable and submitted that there is no application of mind of the Authority and that while dealing with the State property a duty is cast upon the Authority to show a reasonable care and must not be arbitrary and should be transparent and needs certain standard of carrying with the statutory principles and has referred to Robsons and Fleming Report regarding the setting up of terminal submitted to Chittagong Port Authority. The learned Counsel has submitted with reference to the Annexure-I to the writ petition that what approval has been set for on the proposal was BOO project as is evident from proposal dated 19-12-1997 together with approval of the authority for 99 years lease as to BOO project Annexure-J. The learned Counsel has further (submitted with reference to summary presented before the Prime Minister showing the same to be BOO project for 99 years which is reiterated by the agreement dated 17-12-1998 between BIWTA and the Company in respect of Pangaon terminal. The learned Counsel has submitted with reference to the comment on the implementation agreement under Annexure-H by the Chittagong Port Authority about the non-transparency of the project and that the project is a largesse to the Company on the part of the Government is apparent from implementation agreement that the same though a BOO project for 30 years with a rider clause for renewal of another 30 years but the effective date of the project being uncertain and without a specific commencing date of giving effect, the entire project is not transparent. The learned Counsel has submitted that the nature of the BOT being competition tender process, ownership of Berth Water area as licensee, applicable of all laws of the land including the provisions of CPA Ordinance and Customs Act, provision for audited statement of bidders and that the provision for effective date of execution of the 30 years BOT being uncertain in the instant case, the entire transaction with the petitioner was not transparent. The learned Counsel has submitted with reference to the report of the parliamentary committee to show that the authority has ignored the said committee and kept it in the dark regarding the affairs of the project in respect of its query of certain vital issues in the national interest. Instead, a committee has been formed with certain Government officials and in hot-haste, without examining the pros and cons of the project in the interest of the country, proceeded to draw up an implementation agreement in order to accommodate the company for giving undue benefit to the latter. 

 9. Khandkar Mahbubuddin Ahmed, the learned Counsel appearing for the petitioner, further submitted with reference to impugned Annexures-J, K and L that the High Court Division traveled beyond these Annexures and tried to make out a case challenging certain other annexures of subsequent dates and beyond the scope thereof. The learned Counsel has submitted that the challenge was up to the approval of the project and not beyond so as to include the implementation agreement which has not been impugned in the Rule, could not be attracted or challenged in order to avoid any miscarriage in the matter of disposal of the Rule. The learned Counsel has submitted that the project is BOT on expiry of its 30 years with provision for renewal for further 30 years from the effective dates and has referred to the matrix of commercial principles to be reflected in the implementation agreement inasmuch as there is no law that BOT cannot be for 30 years with a provision for further renewal for 30 years. The learned Counsel has further submitted that it is not true that a largesse is given away to the company. 

 21. On the face of the decision of the Ministry of Shipping requiring particulars/ information to be collected from elsewhere including the neighbouring countries in order to formulate the terms and conditions for a competitive bid by inviting international tenders the arbitrary approval of an incorporated proposal of the writ respondent No. 8 has surely acted and/or operated against the interest of the country and such a move of impugned approval by the Government smacks mala fide at the behest of the interested quarters in obtaining the approval. 

 22. It has been alleged by the writ petitioners that no evaluation of the track record of the company i.e. the previous experience of SSA Bangladesh Ltd, or its national component regarding Port operations, financial capability or feasibility study, had been given serious consideration before the hot-haste approval of their proposal inasmuch as no technical and financial evaluation was done about SSA Bangladesh Ltd and there was even no ascertainment of these aspects which were allegedly done at the behest of the interested SSA Bangladesh Ltd without considering any other available proposals or through evaluating other bids received or inviting further competitive bids. 

 28. We have also been apprised of the extracts from the proceedings of the Parliamentary Standing Committee regarding granting of approval in favour of SSA Bangladesh Ltd. It appears that the committee made detailed discussion on the issue and has approved certain decision on 13-12-2000 as under: 

 34. Dr Kamal Hossain, appearing on behalf of the respondents, submitted that High Court Division was correct in holding that the approval had been given arbitrarily, without application of mind, unreasonably and against public interest inasmuch as the approval had been given without evaluating the past record of SSA Bangladesh Limited, financial soundness of the company and its partner-shareholders and the feasibility of the project without following a competitive bidding procedure or maintaining transparency. 

 35. The learned Counsel has referred to a decision of the Ministry requiring information to be collected from neighbouring countries on the basis of which terms and conditions were to be formulated Sand competitive bids were to be invited by public advertisement. This decision was completely ignored by the authorities responsible for granting the approval. The World Bank's expert consultants (Robson & Fleming) specifically dealt with the proposed terminal project at Patenga and expressly recommended on 23 October, 1996 that a two-stage process would be appropriate for it. Pre-qualification and competitive bids to be invited from pre-qualified parties for development on BOT basis based on a feasibility study and term should be of around 30 years but the recommendation was also not considered. 

 38. The aforesaid queries, principles and anxieties of the Chittagong Port Authority over the implementation agreement and the matrix for the approval of the project in favour of the petitioner are well found and genuine which have not been attended to or addressed by the Authority/committee engaged in implementation of the project could not be repelled by the Authority and, on the contrary, it appears that despite the objection of the CP Authority, the Government has been proceeding ahead with the finalisation of the said defective and unrealistic implementation agreement. 

 39. It is to be noted here that the Chittagong Port Authority is responsible under the Chittagong Port Ordinance, 1976 for the management, maintenance, supervision and development of Chittagong Port and for matters connected and incidental thereto and has a duty to approve any such project like establishment of Container Terminals but by usurping its Authority and in disregard of the provision of the CP Ordinance the alleged approval has been given which is ex facie illegal, malafide and without any lawful authority. 

 40. It is further submitted by the writ-petitioner-respondents that no feasibility study for setting up of a Private Container Terminal having been held the Government move of impugned approval without such study for setting up of a Container Terminal at the mouth of the river Karnafuli having Naval Academy, Air force installation and an International Airport is hazardous from the point of view of the security and the approval of the Government without such study is arbitrary and without any lawful authority and manifests non-application of mind at the behest of the interested quarter inasmuch as the Authority while dealing with State Property, a duty is cast to show that the process must not be arbitrary and non-transparent and should follow the salutary principle that certain normal standard of fairness should be there in the matter of executing the process. 

 "On scrutiny of the aforesaid government file which contains the notes, papers and documents relating to impugned approval we could not find any paper or legal document to show cause Stevedoring Services of America of USA has any connection with the writ-respondent No. 8 company and/or with the SSA Netherland BV, the foreign shareholder of the writ-respondent No. 8 company. No note or paper or document was available in the file to confirm the identity or the status of SSA Netherland BV. It appears that no copy or attempt was made to get any information regarding the status and identity of SSA Netherland BV. No paper or financial analysis or break-up as to the estimated profit and loss account on yearly basis of the proposed project showing the expected profit amount payable to Bangladesh was available in the file or in the said two volumes. There was neither any project profile or viability report of the proposed project nor any paper/document showing financial soundness, experience and capability of the SSA Netherland BV to justify to be a partner in the Joint Venture Company for setting up the proposed container terminals in Bangladesh was available in the file. In the absence of aforesaid information no person of prudence will normally take any step of the impugned approval that was initiated without application of mind and negligently. The letter dated 29-12-1997, as it appears, could at best be treated a letter showing interest and in reply to which the Ministry of Shipping ought to have asked the Writ-respondent No. 8 to submit a detailed project proposal with financial analysis formally, which the Ministry has done in the case of Overseas Trade Services, as evidenced by Annexure-Z-6 to the affidavit in reply dated 31-7-2002." 

 "We are surprised to note that the government officials treated the application dated 29-12-1997 as a project proposal in spite of the fact that the application was not accompanied with any project profile, feasibility/viability report on proposed project showing the financial analysis in respect of the investments/expenditures detailing the major heads of accounts, particularly the expenses to be incurred for construction of the covered area and uncovered area and showing the expected income from the project on completion thereof and the amount, out of the expected income from the project, to be paid to the Government of Bangladesh. Without knowing about the financial benefits to be received by the Government, it cannot be said that the concerned government officers acted fairly and reasonably or prudently in considering the proposal of the writ-respondent No. 8 and initiating a file for approval of such inadequate and incomplete offer." 

 43. It appears from the letter dated 29-12-1997 praying for permission to proceed with the operational plan for establishment of Container Terminals in Private Sector in Dhaka and Chittagong under Build, Own and Operate basis and approval was for acquisition of 250 acres of land with 1500 metres of water front at Patenga point for Patenga Container Terminal including Waterfront land of Chittagong Port Authority and for Pangaon with waterfront land of BIWTA adjacent to the proposed land on outright sale and on lease basis together with approval for acquisition of 88.835 acres of land at Pangaon acquired by BIWTA for development of Pangaon Container Terminal including 4.3 Km of excess road land. 

 51. But the writ-respondent No. 1, SSA Bangladesh Ltd, has been registered as a Company illegally suppressing the fact that SSA Netherlands BV, the promoter Netherlands Company allegedly subscribed the Articles of Association of the writ-respondent No. 8 Company and the papers submitted before the Registrar of Joint Stock Companies and other authorities including the application dated 28-12-1997 for approval was a non-existent Company in between 1-12-1997 and 28-4-1998 but was allegedly incorporated on 30-5-2001 and again by a resolution dated 20-6-2001 decided to wind up SSA Netherlands BV which proceeding attained its finality on 17-12-2001. Thus, it appears that the alleged transfer of shares by SSA. Netherlands BV on 4-12-2001 in favour of SSA Holding Bangladesh Inc. Cayman Island is a fraudulent and illegal transaction made during the period when SSA Netherlands BV was undergoing winding up proceedings. Thus, the allotment of shares in the SSA Netherlands BV, a non-existent Company by the writ-respondent No. 8 Company and subsequent treating SSA Netherlands BV as its shareholder is a fraud perpetuated on the Authorities concerned including the Government, BOI, and the Registrar of Joint Stock Companies, etc. with ulterior motive best known to the promoters of the said alleged joint venture Company inasmuch as the entire transaction was misleading, motivated, not through a fair process and ex facie illegal and malafide. 

 "Apart from this, we have found that the writ-respondent No. 8 company has been registered illegally as a company since formed With one legal shareholder only inasmuch as the foreign shareholder of the Joint Venture Company, namely SSA Netherlands BV, was nonexistent in the eye of law on the date writ-respondent No. 8 company was incorporated i.e. on 15-12-1997, and the allotments of shares in favour of SSA Netherlands were made illegally, since being not in existence and therefore the registration of the project of the illegally formed writ-respondent No. 8 company by the Board of Investment is void and accordingly, the approval of the proposed project in favour of the Writ-respondent No. 8 is void ab initio and consequently, the subsequent process and or actions based on the void approval of the proposal are illegal and without lawful authority" 

 59. In the case of ETV Ltd vs Dr Chowdhury Mahmud Hasan reported in 54 DLR (AD) 130 wherein the Licensing agreement dated 9-3-1999 signed by and between Ministry of Information, the respondent No. 1 and Mr AS Mahmud respondent No. 7 and the subsequent approval of transfer of the said licence to the ETV Ltd were challenged to have been entered with and granted unlawfully and without lawful authority and to be of no legal effect, it has been held, inter alia, that: 

 60. It appears from Annexure-I that the writ-respondent No. 8-petitioner made the proposal on 19-12-1997 as a BOO project, the BOI by its letter dated 13-1-1998 accorded the registration and that the Council Committee in its meeting on 25-3-1998 recommended for approval of the Prime Minister and on 26-4-1998 the Prime Minister approved the project directing the Ministry of Shipping for implementation of the project and on 28-4-1998 the Ministry of Shipping issued the letter of approval without considering the feasibility study of the project and settling the terms considering the project to be one as BOO, the aforesaid steps/process in a hot-haste manner without sufficient materials required for infrastructure project like the present one, manifests a shady deal in the matter of alleged approval resulting in an abuse of executive power at the behest of the writ-respondent No. 8 petitioner which requires accountability or transparency in according the approval. 

 61. It is to be remembered that the authority has a duty to scrutinise the process of approval of the infrastructure project which, in the facts and circumstances of the case, has been breached in discharging public duty causing injury to the public at large. 

 66. In the instant case though a contract has not yet been entered into as yet but the process that has been adopted in the matter of approval of the project being not fair, reasonable or according to the established principles of law or practice or procedure, we are of the view that the impugned action is malafide, arbitrary, unfair, unreasonable and does not have the sanction of any law or norms. 

 "It is now well settled that the State property may be in the form of legal right and in the nature of privilege. The government largesse known as privileges is now regarded as rights and the government cannot enter into any agreement in respect of its largesse arbitrarily or at its absolute discretion and it is also in the practice that in the event of allowing any such right, the normal procedure is to call for competitive bids to get a better price and to show fairness on the part of the authority in the instant case, in view of the availability of the parties interested in setting up of container terminals, at least during the relevant period, the authority ought to have gone for competitive bids, more so when no specific amount of the expected money was mentioned in the letter of the writ-respondent No. 8 dated 29-12-1997, which Bangladesh would get from the earning by the proposed project. This indicates arbitrariness on the part of the government officials involved in proceeding with the file and notes for the impugned approval. The government officials involved in the process of the impugned approval thus appears to have acted not only negligently but also acted arbitrarily for the benefit of a private party, and against the public interest."
